name: gather_context
description: Use for a task that needs evidence from several places, such as a change that spans implementation and tests, even when the task names a symbol; call again with narrower needs as you learn more. Pass the task text as task, and optionally needs, anchors, deliverable and known. Returns a short map: for each need, where it is answered and the best passages, and what was not found. A code_change or test deliverable, or stated needs, also gathers the project rules, how tests run and the build file, and lists any it does not find. Ranges listed without text can be read with read_indexed_range. For one definition use find_definition; for one known file, outline_file. response_mode=full returns the complete reply.

calls.description: Canonical reads over the whole Answer.

candidates.description: Candidate records over the whole Answer, before dedup.

fanout.description: Peak concurrent reads in one round of one part.

input_tokens.description: Model input token pool of the whole attempt.

max_bytes.description:
Bytes retained while gathering; the reply takes at most the smaller
of this and 131,072 bytes.

round_input_tokens.description: Model input tokens of one round of one part.

Deliverable.description: What the caller will produce from the gathered context.

KnownRange.description: A repository-relative path, whole or with inclusive one-based lines.

anchors.description:
Up to 16 exact strings to look for (identifiers, routes, quoted text,
numbers with units), each at most 200 UTF-8 bytes. Take them from the
task or from evidence an earlier reply returned.

budget.description:
The loop's limits (calls, deadline_ms, max_bytes and the rest). Omit
with task for the service default; a valid budget is used as sent.
Required with question.

continuation.description: A ticket or continuation id, to attach to an existing job.

deliverable.description:
What you will produce. code_change also gathers the project rules, how
tests run, the build file and where errors reach the user; test, the
first three.

fresh.description: Start an independent run; never reuse a job by digest.

include_status.description: Include current freshness/readiness even when unchanged on this connection.

interactive.description:
The job may run to completion with no caller waiting. It never ranks
a job ahead of an attended one.

invocation_key.description: Exact retry recovery within the caller's own scope.

known.description:
Up to 32 path ranges you already hold. They are validated only; they
do not yet change what is gathered or returned.

needs.description:
Up to 8 statements of what you must learn, one per need, each at most
400 UTF-8 bytes. Stated needs also gather the project rules, how tests
run and the build file.

question.description: Existing full request only, with schema and budget; never with task.

reply_detail.description: Lean/Rich changes available fact projection, never retention. Reads without an alternate projection keep their existing payload. Omission preserves legacy defaults; conflicts with compact reject. Search full_chunks is independent.

response_mode.description: Terse is the default. Full adds provenance, coverage and readiness detail; for gather_context it is the complete reply, including passages the short map leaves out. It does not widen the search.

schema.description: Existing full request only; supplied by the service for task.

task.description: The whole task in your words; it becomes the question.

verification.description: Report is the default: bounded dated saved-byte outcomes. Off skips source checks; require fails unless every returned file reference matches. No extraction, completeness or unsaved-buffer certification.

verification_deadline_ms.description: Cooperative deadline, 1..120000 ms; default 2000. Blocking filesystem calls retain capacity until they return.

wait_ms.description: How long this call waits; never shortens the job.
